title: Servers, routing and MVC
subtitle: What happens on the other side of the request: routing, business logic, the database and the response.

sections.title: Request → response
sections.body: A server listens on a port, parses the request, routes it to a handler, does the work (read/write a database, call services), and builds a response. A minimal Node handler: app.get('/hello', (req, res) => res.send('hi')).

choices.text: A method and path to a handler.

sections.title: Middleware
sections.body: Middleware are functions that see every request in order: logging, parsing JSON, authentication, then the route handler; each may respond or call next(). Order matters: authentication must run before the handler it protects.

questions.prompt: Where must an authentication middleware sit?

figures.caption: Figure 3.2.1 — middleware chain
figures.note: Auth sits before the handler; a bad token would stop here.

sections.title: MVC
sections.body: Model: data and business rules; View: templates that render HTML; Controller: maps requests to model calls and picks a view. The router hands a request to the controller, which asks the model, then renders a view.

figures.caption: Figure 3.3.1 — MVC with a database

sections.title: Databases from code
sections.body: Use parameterised queries — never build SQL by pasting user input. An ORM maps tables to classes. Cache hot reads (Redis) and index the columns you filter by.

worked.why: A product lookup takes 20 ms from the database, 1 ms from cache. 90 % of reads hit the cache.

questions.prompt: A cache hit rate of 90 % makes average read time…

problems.prompt: Cache 2 ms, DB 40 ms, hit rate 75 %. Average time?

sections.title: State: cookies and sessions
sections.body: HTTP is stateless, so after login the server issues a session id in a cookie; the browser sends it with every request and the server looks up the session. Cookies should be HttpOnly (not readable by JS), Secure (HTTPS only) and SameSite.

figures.caption: Figure 3.5.1 — session login
figures.note: The cookie is the only thing the browser remembers.

sections.title: Scaling a server
sections.body: Add servers behind a load balancer; keep servers stateless (sessions in a shared store) so any can answer. Put static files on a CDN. If one server handles 200 requests/s, how many for 1500 req/s with 25 % headroom?
